item.title: Sharon Osbourne Marks First Wedding Anniversary Without Ozzy: ‘Forever My Heart’
item.description:
[Eerie music fades out, and a gentle, nostalgic tune takes over]
Host: Welcome to this special episode of "Trending on Billboard". Today, we're remembering a rock legend and celebrating a love that transcends time. On July 4th, Sharon Osbourne marked what would have been her 46th wedding anniversary with the late Ozzy Osbourne.
[Soft music continues to play in the background]
Host: Sharon shared a heartfelt tribute to Ozzy on Instagram, alongside a sweet photo of the couple holding hands. She wrote, "Today would have been our 46th wedding anniversary. Instead, it is a celebration of a love that even death could not diminish." Ozzy passed away on July 22, 2025, at the age of 76, after a brave battle with Parkinson's disease.
[Music transitions to a brief clip of Ozzy's "Crazy Train"]
Host: But even in death, Ozzy's music lives on. After his passing, his songs saw a significant surge on the Billboard charts. "Crazy Train" debuted on the Hot 100 for the first time, and "Mama, I'm Coming Home" re-entered the chart after 33 years. His compilation, "The Essential Ozzy Osbourne", reached new heights on the Billboard 200, and he dominated the Top Rock & Alternative Albums charts.
[Music transitions back to the gentle, nostalgic tune]
Host: Ozzy's legacy is a testament to his enduring impact on rock music. With over 100 million albums sold worldwide, he claimed nine solo top 10 entries on the Billboard 200 and scored two top 10 Hot 100 hits. Black Sabbath's reunion album "13" even gave the band their first-ever Billboard 200 No. 1 in 2013.
[Music fades out, and the host speaks in a gentle tone]
Host: As we remember Ozzy Osbourne, we're reminded that true love and great music can leave a lasting legacy that transcends time. Thank you for tuning in to this special episode of "Trending on Billboard". Until next time, farewell.
